title: Max-flow criterion via incrementing paths
statement: Let $N$ be a network — a finite digraph carrying a nonnegative integer capacity on each arc, with disjoint nonempty source and sink sets and a distinguished source $x$ and sink $y$ — and let $f$ be a flow in $N$. Then $f$ is a maximum flow if and only if there is no $f$-incrementing path in $N$ ending at the sink $y$.
hypotheses_covered: N is a network (finite digraph with integer arc capacities, disjoint nonempty source set X and sink set Y, distinguished source x and sink y)
f is a flow in N
caveat: The predicate IncPath (f-incrementing path to y) is used in the statement but its definition was not supplied among the given upstream definitions; I have rendered it by its standard meaning — a path along which the flow f can be augmented, terminating at the distinguished sink y.
replaced:
\emph{A flow \texttt{f} in \texttt{N} is a maximum flow if and only if \texttt{N}
contains no \texttt{f}-incrementing path.}
